sections.text: Intelligence, wisdom, non-illusion, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calmness, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear and fearlessness;
Harmlessness, equanimity, contentment, austerity, beneficence, fame and failure, all these, the characteristics of beings, spring from Me only.

The seven Great Seers, the Progenitors of mankind, the Ancient Four, and the Lawgivers were born of My Will and come forth direct from Me. The race of mankind has sprung from them. [ Mareechi, Atri, Angira, Pulah, Kratu, Pulastya, Vahishta. The Masters: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan, Sanatkumar.]

We have been discussing Chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, Yoga of divine Glories. We have seen so far that Bhagavan is immanent as well as transcendental. Bhagavan is immanent because he resides in the hearts of all beings , Ishvara Sarva Bhutanam Hrideshe Arjuna Tishtathi. Ishvara is residing in the hearts of all beings, therefore immanent. But hes also transcendental because we do not recognize him.
This chapter started out by Bhagavan saying in the second verse, I am not known to anyone. Neither the Devas, the divine beings or the divine senses, know me, nor the Great Rishis know me. He is not known by the mind or the intellect. By applying the normal tools of my cognition, I cannot know Ishvara. Therefore he is transcendental. So these two aspects of Bhagavan we have to overcome, in a sense, to know Him.
We have to find altar of meditation. We have completed the first segment of karma yoga, culminated in a Dhyana Yoga to meditate upon that supreme Self, my true Self. But what to meditate upon is what we have been discussing since last three chapters 7, 8 and 9. And Bhagawan in various ways told us what his real nature is that I am all pervading. Everything is strung into me. There is no reality other than me.
But its still difficult for us to meditate on those aspects of Bhagavan. So the Vibhuti Yoga, the glories of the Lord, are required to meditate upon, to focus on. Something which I can identify through the limited means that I have, is my mind and intellect. So in this chapter, the Bhagavan is giving us the Vibhuti, that which I can identify and vouch for his presence. It is something like when I am in a deep sleep at night and wake up suddenly if I really want to know whether the sun is outside or not. That means, is it a day or not?
When I open my windows and I see sunlight, I do not see the sun, but I see sunlight. The presence of sunlight tells me that sun has risen. The sun is there outside. I may not be able to see sun for various reasons. Maybe a building is blocking my view, maybe so bright that I cannot see it. But the very fact that I can experience the sunlight, it tells me that sun has risen.
In the same way, if I know the Vibhutis Sri Bhagawan says, if you can identify the qualities which emanate from me, which are my real qualities, then you should be able to vouch for my presence. The Lord resides in all hearts, in all beings, in all things. But I cannot vouch for it right now. So Bhagawan is giving us the tools to realize his presence. So in verse 3, Bhagavan concluded Yomam Ajam Anadim, Chaviti, Loka Maheshwaram. I am not known to the Devas.
I am also not known to the Rishis, the great sages. I am not known through intellect nor I am known through mind. However, if one knows that I am Ajam Anadim, I am the source of all being. I am birthless and beginningless. It is uncaused, caused, then it is birthless. There is nothing before me.
Therefore there is nothing is causing my existence. And also Im beginningless because theres nothing before me. Loka Maheshwaram, the Lord of all the entire creation is there because of me. Because of the entity which is beginningless and birthless, the entire Jagat exists, the Bhagavan, the Lord Ishvara is the material cause and efficient cause for this Jagat. When he created this universe out of his own Maya, there was no other material available to him. From his own self, from his own qualities.
He provided the material as well as the knowledge, the efficient cause to create this Jagat. So the creation, if it all comes out of he is the Loka Maheshram. He is the Lord of all the beings. Lord is the one on whom my existence depends. So my Lord is my own consciousness. Without that, my existence as this limited being does not exist.
The day consciousness is not there, I will not be nil Bhatt. Ill be just a dead body. So Bhagavan said Asammudasam, the one who is not deluded by these appearances, he will be relieved of all the sins. In other words, all the ignorances, all the ignorant ideas that I have about myself as a limited being, Ill be liberated from. And then he enumerates those 20 qualities of the supreme Being, the divinity. These qualities in people, in things and beings, exist because of my presence. Those qualities are somewhat easy to understand.
Buddhi, Gnanam, Asamoha, Shamah, Satyam, Damaha, Shamaha. Buddhi is intellect, Nischayatmika Buddhi , that which decides what is right and wrong. So when I feel that Im exhibiting my Buddhi because I can decide it is day and not night, thats my Buddhi. Bhagavan says that because of my presence in you, this Buddhi exists in you at the microcosm. This Buddhi I use for deciding whats outside in this world. Gnanam , this Buddhi now gives me knowledge of what is real and what is unreal.
Asammoha and non illusion. When I have Buddhi and I apply it to find out whether it is day outside or night, when I wake up, it gives me non illusion. Even though it was dark in my room, there is no difference between day and night in my room. But as soon as I open the window, I knew its a day outside. That is because of my Buddhi that if there is sunlight outside, the sun has risen and therefore it is a day. So that created a Samohaha.
Non-illusion, no delusion, no confusion. Out of these three, I develop other qualities such as Kshama (forgiveness), Satyam (truth), Damaha (control of the Indriyas), and Shamaha (control of the mind). Weve seen in Tattva Bodh that Shamah is Mano Nigrahaha, and Damaha is control of the senses such as eyes and ears. Now, if I see that somebody is not yet convinced that its day outside , even though I have concluded that it is day , if my wife doesnt agree with me, then I forgive her.
I think she has not seen outside yet. Because of my knowledge, my Buddhi, my non-delusion, I can forgive other people who are still not at that level. She has not woken up completely. She cannot see the light outside , to her, its still night. I can forgive her because of my knowledge.
If I have no knowledge, there will be confusion. We will be fighting about it. But because I have knowledge, I can have Kshama and I can vouch for the truth that it is day outside. I can control my actions and also my mind. All this emanates from the same source , my own consciousness at the vyashti, at the microcosm. I have all these exhibiting through me.
Because of that divinity, the consciousness functioning through me, Im identifying with it. Sukham Dukham Bhavah Abhavah, Bhayam cha Abhayam eva cha. These are the pairs of opposites I have to deal with in this world , this world which I have created out of my own consciousness. In deep sleep, there was no world outside to deal with. There were no pairs of opposites.
There was no confusion about day or night. But as soon as I woke up and I have this Buddhi and Gnana exhibiting through me. Now I have to deal with this world outside which has pairs of opposites. So Kannadukha Bhava and Abhava. Existence and non existence, birth and death. Bhayam cha Bhayam Bhaya is a positive emotion which protects me from getting myself hurt.
If I have no Bhaya of jumping from a third floor window, then Im going to hurt myself. So this fear of getting hurt is actually protecting me. So therefore its a positive emotion. And Abhaya and fearlessness. Things which I am very sure about. Ill be fearless no matter what.
Somebody tells me that I do not exist. So things which I so sure about my existence, Im fearless. Things which Im not sure about my existence. After my death, Im fearful. I have fear of death because I have no idea what will happen after my death. Im fearless about my existence right now.
Because I know who I am and how I exist exist. So theres both fear and fearlessness emanating from my identification with my consciousness. Ahimsa, non injury, Samatha, equanimity, Tusthi, contentment, Tapaha, disciplines, austerity, Dhanam, charity, Yashaha, Fame and also Ayyashaha ill fame. All these I experience because of my identification with myself as my conscious conscious being. These 20 qualities are given as the glories of that supreme Lord. These are the basic qualities through which he manifests in this world through beings.
He resides in the hearts of all the beings. And when those beings identify with him, these positive qualities are exhibited through them. Then what about the opposites of this? Like Hinsa, Abudhi, Agnana, Samoha. It is nothing but non identification with the self. When I identify with the Divinity within me, all these positive qualities of the divinity will be manifesting through me.
When Im not identifying with that divinity, then the lack of those qualities will be exhibiting. So the lack of qualities are not really any qualities. They are just lack of good qualities. Something similar to how there is nothing called cold , just a lack of heat. Heat I can identify as a form of energy, but cold has no form of energy.
It just lack of heat creates sensation of cold. Lack of Ahimsa creates Himsa. Lack of Buddhi creates Abuddhi , one who doesnt know anything. Lack of knowledge creates ignorance. So the negatives which we see in this world is because of non identification with the true self. Bhagavan said this entire Jagat is created by my own mind using my own self as the material.
My Maya is the material, therefore he is the Loka Maheshwaram. Without him no world is possible. Without you being conscious of your world, your world cannot exist. Without me being conscious of my world, my world does not exist. And therefore he, the Supreme Lord who is functioning through all beings as their consciousness. He is the Lord of all all the beings.
So he is justifying why he is Loka, Maheshwaram, Bhavanti, Bhava, Bhutana, Mata Eva, Pruthakvida. These varieties of expressions you see in this world through various beings with all these qualities in the various levels, this permutation combinations, all these 20 qualities creates this multitude of personalities in this world. Somebody has more Buddhi, somebody has more Kshama, somebody has more Ahimsa. All these manifestations in this world through beings. But anytime I see the expression of any of these qualities, I must know that divinity is present in that being. Bhavanti Bhava Bhutanam Mata Eva Prithak Vidhaha.
All these different kinds of qualities of being arise from me alone. Without that one common thread which we call it consciousness, life, none of these are possible. And therefore we should know when we see these qualities that the Lord is present. And therefore when we meet each other, when we see the exhibition of any of these qualities, we have to do Namaste that I see the divinity in you is emanating through you as kindness. All these qualities are nothing but the glories of the Lord and Bhagawan. Meditate on those glories.
These are your means, the tools for you to meditate on the divine self that you are. Then Bhagavan concludes by giving a complete picture of the creation. Maharsayah, Saptapurve, Chatvarohu, Manamahata, Madbhava Manasa Jata, Esam, Loka, Imah, Prajaha.

These verses reveal twenty divine qualities that emanate from the Lords presence: Buddhi (intellect), Jnana (wisdom), Asamoha (non-delusion), Kshama (forgiveness), Satya (truth), Dama (sense-control), Shama (mind-control), Sukha and Dukha (pleasure and pain), Bhava and Abhava (birth and death), Bhaya and Abhaya (fear and fearlessness), Ahimsa (non-injury), Samata (equanimity), Tushti (contentment), Tapa (austerity), Dana (charity), Yasha and Ayasha (fame and ill-fame). Each of these exists in beings only because of the divine presence within. When we see someone display wisdom, forgiveness, or fearlessness, we are witnessing the Lords light shining through that individual.
The teaching also clarifies something crucial: negative qualities are simply the absence of these positive divine expressions. Just as cold is not a thing in itself but merely the absence of heat, ignorance is the absence of knowledge, cruelty is the absence of compassion. This understanding transforms how we view both ourselves and others - rather than seeing bad as a positive force, we recognize it as non-identification with our divine nature. Today, when you encounter any of these twenty qualities in yourself or others - a moment of genuine forgiveness, an act of charity, a flash of wisdom - pause and recognize: This is divinity expressing itself.
Reflect on these questions: Which of these twenty qualities do I most naturally express? Which ones feel distant from me? Can I see even difficult emotions like fear or the experience of loss as part of the divine tapestry of existence, present only because consciousness is present?
